name: Windows Development
notes: Builds go through manage_build; manage_editor has no build action. The `target` field above is Unity's BuildTarget name, while manage_build's `target` param takes the bridge alias (`windows64`) -- see bridgeCall. `scripting_backend` accepts only `mono` or `il2cpp`; there is no `coreclr` value, so a CoreCLR backend cannot be selected through the bridge. The `options` array accepts only clean_build, auto_run, deep_profiling, compress_lz4, strict_mode and detailed_report. `allowDebugging` has no bridge option of its own -- it follows from `development: true`. `scenes` is passed as a JSON array string, not a native array.
